doc.title: Frank Foster and Bill Hughes interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Schenectady, New York, March 28, 1995

title: The band refuses to play for Titus Turner
summary: Hughes tells how the band sat silent behind singer Titus Turner while Basie enjoyed it.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Yeah. There was another time, you remember Titus Turner?

Titus Turner was a singer of sorts, and he was performing with the band. And I don’t know what he did to get everybody upset. But everybody was very upset at Titus. And somebody cooked up the plot: we ain’t playing, you know, behind this guy. And I think Marhsall kicked off the tune, and all of a sudden everybody was just sitting there.
And everybody was just sitting there and this guy, he was so upset he started crying. And Basie was dying over there, you know?
No, I don’t remember his crying.
The band refused to play for him. And Basie died. And he was looking at him like “I told you.”
